recent_posts.title: DuckDuckGo's New Pro Plan: 2x AI Limits, More Advanced Models
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo has launched a new Pro subscription tier at $19.99/month or $199.99/year, sitting above the existing Plus plan ($9.99/month). The Pro plan offers three Duck.ai upgrades: 2x higher usage limits compared to Plus (covering text chat, voice chat, and image generation), exclusive access to Claude Opus 4.6, and extended reasoning capabilities on both GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6. The existing subscription is now rebranded as Plus. Both plans include a VPN, Personal Information Removal, and Identity Theft Restoration. Free users retain access to a set of base models with daily limits. Subscriptions are available in the US, Canada, EU, and UK.

recent_posts.title: 2025 DuckDuckGo Charitable Donations: $1.1M to privacy and digital competition non-profits around the world
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo announces $1.1 million in charitable donations for 2025, bringing their total contributions since 2011 to over $8 million. The donations support 29 organizations worldwide focused on privacy rights, digital competition, and online security, including major recipients like Public Knowledge ($100k), ARTICLE 19 ($75k), and the Electronic Frontier Foundation ($50k). Organizations range from policy advocacy groups and digital rights defenders to open source security projects and anti-monopoly initiatives.

recent_posts.title: DuckDuckGo subscription adds advanced AI chat models
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo has expanded its subscription service to include access to advanced AI models like GPT-4o, GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, and Llama Maverick through Duck.ai. The subscription remains $9.99/month and includes VPN, personal information removal, and identity theft restoration services. Duck.ai provides privacy-focused AI chat with anonymized conversations, no AI training on user data, local storage, and instant deletion capabilities. The basic Duck.ai service remains free, with premium models available only to subscribers.

recent_posts.title: DuckDuckGo Privacy Pro launches 7 day free trial with major updates
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo launches 7-day free trials for Privacy Pro, their subscription service combining VPN, personal information removal, and identity theft restoration. Major updates include international availability across US, EU, Canada, and UK, expanded VPN server locations in 30+ countries, independent security audit results, automatic blocking of malicious domains, and improved personal information removal covering 80+ data broker sites. The service costs $9.99/month or $99.99/year after the trial period.

recent_posts.title: DuckDuckGo browser gets visual refresh with new design and AI integration
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo has released a visual refresh for its browser featuring redesigned icons, softer interface elements, and a new color palette. The update includes improved tracking protection indicators, easier access to Duck.ai (their private AI chat feature), and better cross-platform consistency between desktop and mobile versions. Users can optionally enable or disable AI features through browser settings.

recent_posts.title: DuckDuckGo Scam Blocker Expands to Include More Threats
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo has expanded its built-in Scam Blocker to protect against more online threats including fake e-commerce sites, cryptocurrency scams, and scareware. Unlike other browsers that use Google's Safe Browsing service and share data with Google, DuckDuckGo's solution works anonymously using threat data from Netcraft. The feature blocks phishing sites, malware, malicious ads, and various scam sites without tracking user browsing data. It's free and enabled by default in the DuckDuckGo browser, with Privacy Pro subscribers getting full-device protection through VPN.

recent_posts.title: DuckDuckGo’s AI Features: Private, Useful and Optional
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo launches free, private access to popular AI chatbots via Duck.ai, as well as expanded AI-assisted answers on its search engine. Features include upgraded chatbot models and the ability to store chats locally. Users can customize the frequency of AI-assisted answers and enjoy the privacy of having no data collected or used for training AI models.

recent_posts.title: Roadblocks to Competition: Investigate Google’s Non-Compliance with the EU’s Digital Markets Act
recent_posts.summary: The post calls for the European Commission to investigate Google's non-compliance with several articles of the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA). The DMA mandates Google to share anonymized click and query data, implement choice screens for users to easily change default search settings, and ensure downloaded search or browser apps can prompt users to set search defaults easily. The post highlights how Google’s selective compliance and inadequate proposals undermine these objectives, emphasizing the need for formal investigations to ensure fair competition in the search market.

recent_posts.title: Investing in privacy-respecting companies that are raising the standard of trust online
recent_posts.summary: DuckDuckGo is investing in early-stage companies that focus on enhancing consumer privacy. The company donates to non-profit organizations and seeks partnerships or acquisitions with like-minded entrepreneurs. Current focus areas include search and browsing, consumer privacy technologies, and emerging technologies like private AI chatbots. Contact Mike Marino, SVP of Finance, or Diana Chiu, Director of Corporate & Business Development, for more information.

recent_posts.title: Creating Enduring Competition in the Search Market
recent_posts.summary: Antitrust measures are proposed to counter Google's dominance in the search market. DuckDuckGo suggests legal and technical interventions including providing fair access to Google's search results via real-time APIs, banning Google's exclusive default agreements on Chrome and Android, and restricting exclusionary contracts. These combined remedies aim to promote competition and innovation by levelling the playing field for rival search engines. Historical precedents and regulatory oversight will be crucial for implementing and monitoring these measures effectively.
